zeroconf_confirm.title: Vurio found
zeroconf_confirm.description: Vurio answers at {url}. Make an API token in Vurio under Settings → API tokens, with live:view, events:read and recordings:read — and cameras:manage to switch cameras from here — and enter it below.

user.title: Connect to Vurio
user.description: Make an API token in Vurio under Settings → API tokens. It needs live:view; add events:read and recordings:read for events, pictures and recordings, and cameras:manage to switch cameras from here. Each permission is one entry — a token with only recordings:read cannot watch the cameras.

data_description.url: Where Vurio answers, for example http://192.168.1.10:8099.

reauth_confirm.title: Vurio needs a new token
reauth_confirm.description: The API token for {url} was refused. Make a new one in Vurio and enter it here.

reconfigure.title: Change Vurio's address or token
reconfigure.description: For a token with more permissions, make a new one in Vurio under Settings → API tokens — the Home Assistant preset has all four: live:view, events:read, recordings:read and cameras:manage — and enter it here. Entities and dashboards stay as they are.

error.cannot_connect: Vurio could not be reached at that address.
error.missing_permission: The token needs at least live:view. For events, pictures, recordings and switches give it events:read, recordings:read and cameras:manage as well.

abort.already_configured: This Vurio installation is already added.
abort.not_ipv4: Vurio announced an address Home Assistant cannot use; add it by hand.
